notes.title: Release notes v1.7.0 -> 23 January 2025
notes.content:
Hello,
Here we are again with another small batch of fixes. As I start working on another project, I’ll continue integrating minor fixes as players report issues. However, I won’t push updates weekly unless there are enough bugs to keep me busy.


Bug Fixes:

Fixed pan music location to match the character.
Resolved the issue where the menu didn’t open on the first game launch (no idea what happened there!).
Fixed picker AI looping while grabbing something when the pantry is full and added small improvements.
Fixed multiple farm growth and prevented farmers from planting immediately after harvesting (they now usually wait a day, simulating a basic crop rotation).
Fixed the fire hand power, which was no longer working.
Fixed the repair power so that buildings set on fire no longer retain the "on-fire" texture after being repaired.
Made small performance improvements by adding a resource cache for characters to find the closest resource more efficiently.
Fixed a looping issue where characters occasionally got stuck while grabbing objects.
Added small navmesh obstacles around the starting altar to reduce accidents where villagers set themselves on fire.


As always, don’t hesitate to contact me with your feedback!

notes.title: Release notes v1.6.0 -> 19 december 2024
notes.content:
Hello,

This week, I mostly focused on optimization and improving VR controls.

For optimization, it’s nothing huge, but a collection of smaller tweaks that may make a difference, especially on lower-end hardware. I really hope I haven’t broken anything, as I didn’t have time to retest everything thoroughly.

For VR, I completely overhauled the movement controls and some interactions. Movement is now handled with the left thumbstick (you can switch to the right thumbstick in the options). Pressing the thumbstick allows you to rotate—very straightforward.

For VR interactions, you can now play with physical positioning, your hand stays in place instead of zooming to the ground all the time (the old behavior is still available in the options). Grabbing is now performed using the grab button, while powers and flicks still use the trigger button. Many powers now have a fireball-like behavior, where you can throw them around. Unfortunately, I haven’t had time to overhaul all the powers yet.

Everyone:

     Optimized plant growth to limit animations cost in multiple cases like water and rejuvenate.
     Added VFX at the center of the rejuvenate power to help with aiming in VR.
     Added rotation to the scythe when holding the button during the reap power. Very cool in VR.
     Optimized villager AI resource searches.
     Clean up and optimized many low level for-loops in the code.


Only VR:

     Implemented new VR movement method Flying using the headset.
     Implemented new VR movement method Flying using the controller.
     Implemented new VR movement method Teleportation.
 	 Updated tutorial messages to reflect new controls.
     Updated VR controls to assign grabbing to the grab button and flicking to the trigger button.
     Reworked powers to behave like fireballs, with throwable effects and impacts.
     Reworked the reap power to stay put in your hand while active.
     VR UI no longer displays while hovering over an object with an active power in hand.


Bug Fixes (VR):

     Fixed an issue where objects were being planted into the ground when using the trigger while grabbing.
     Quest dialogues are now visible again.
     Fixed VR camera tearing during rotation.


Thanks for reading, and as always, feel free to contact me with any feedback.

I’ll be away from my computer for the holidays until the beginning of January, but I’ll review any new feedback then.

Wishing you all glorious end-of-year celebrations!

notes.title: Hotfixes 01 december 2024
notes.content:
Hello,

Here’s a small update focused primarily on bug fixes. I decided to address the issue of unlocking the fishery, which was blocking other buildings, as it felt too inconvenient to wait for next week’s patch.

Bug Fixes:

     Building Placement: Fixed a bug where buildings could no longer be placed randomly. This was caused by the fishery unlocking without a valid spot available, which blocked the placement of other production buildings. Adjusted the priority order so the fishery is the last to be checked, with other buildings placed based on size.
     Localization Toggle: Added an input option to change the button used for toggling localization from Left Ctrl to any other key, resolving conflicts with player setups.
     Enemy Buildings: Enemy buildings can no longer be moved around using the hand upgrade.
     Gifts: Added camera movements to Sword and Totem gifts so players can see where they spawn. Fixed a bug where the Sword would duplicate after restarting the game.
     Level Power Casting: Fixed an issue where casting the level power on water canceled it and blocked the power wheel display. Now works as expected, allowing other powers to be cast.
     Stockpile Duplication: Unable to consistently reproduce this issue, but I believe I’ve resolved it.
     Fishery Placement: Resolved issues where the fishery spawn failed due to collisions with the water volume, which significantly reduced the range of valid positions.
     Fishery Movement: Fixed multiple issues related to moving the fishery building.
     Fertility Upgrade: Corrected a bug where the upgrade incorrectly allowed unlimited population. The issue arose because the code was reading the max population at 50 instead of the intended upgrade value.


Thanks for reading! As always, feel free to share your feedback.

notes.title: Genesis of a Small God – Release Announcement
notes.content:
Genesis of a Small God – Release Announcement

After over six months in Early Access, I’m thrilled to announce the full release of Genesis of a Small God. This milestone wouldn’t have been possible without the dedication, support, and invaluable feedback from our Early Access players. Each of you has played a crucial role in shaping the game, and it’s thanks to your insights that Genesis of a Small God has reached its current state.

A Special Thanks to Our Community

Reading your feedback and implementing as many of your ideas as possible has been incredibly rewarding. This collaborative approach has been a wonderful experience, and if I have the chance to create another project, I’ll certainly consider Early Access again. I’d love to involve you even earlier in the process, potentially from the initial design phase.

What to Expect at Launch Compared to Early Access

For launch, Genesis of a Small God is in a much more polished state. While I haven’t implemented everything I originally envisioned, I’m proud of the end result. Nearly all known issues have been resolved, aside from those linked directly to the engine. After release, I’ll continue monitoring for any remaining bugs and will address them as well as minor improvements based on your feedback.

Looking Ahead

With the launch, I hope Genesis of a Small God gains more visibility. However, based on early figures and current projections, it’s unlikely that I’ll be able to continue work on additional content or major new features post-launch.

A Few Words on VR Development

The VR version is included, but VR development has brought its own set of unique challenges. I’ve had my fair share of headaches (quite literally!) throughout the process, so I appreciate your patience with any rough edges in this version. While it may not be as polished as I’d hoped, I’m pleased to offer Genesis of a Small God in VR.

Thank you again to everyone who has been part of this journey. As always, don’t hesitate to share your feedback with me!

notes.title: Release notes 08 novembre 2024
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Following recent feedback on performance, I’ve focused mainly on optimizations in this release. It’s frustrating for both players and myself when performance issues arise, especially on high-end hardware.

It appears Unreal Engine 5 is still somewhat immature, causing unpredictable performance results across different systems. Unfortunately, I don’t have the resources to test the game on a wide variety of hardware.

Among the primary culprits are DirectX12 and the default anti-aliasing method, TSR, which can heavily impact performance. To address this, I’ve added video settings so you can adjust these options. If you’re experiencing poor performance on modern hardware, try switching to DirectX11 or changing/disabling anti-aliasing.

For the rendering interface: If you select a different option from the default, you’ll need to restart the game. If the game doesn’t start after changing it, you can revert to default by editing the file located at:
%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\SmallGod\Saved\Config\Windows\Engine.ini
and removing the DefaultGraphicsRHI variable.

    New Features:

         Added a gameplay option to adjust dialogue speed.
         Help messages now display from newest to oldest.


    Optimizations:

         Added RHI selection in video settings for DirectX.
         Added video parameter to change anti-aliasing method.
         Fully disabled static lighting.
         Reduced ground interaction frequency for insect swarms and tornadoes, minimizing unnecessary checks.
         Set actor components to use parent bounds, reducing CPU cost for moving objects.
         Minor improvements to plant growth mechanics, affecting rejuvenate and rain powers.


    Bug Fixes:

         Fixed orb highlighting issues with some ongoing-cost powers.
         Resolved an issue with the painting power that could freeze the game on first use.
         Stopped the orb chime from unnecessarily triggering when recreating the island.
         Corrected level power behavior for single-click versus hold actions.
         Fixed an issue where the game wouldn’t save when exiting the menu using ESC instead of “Continue.”


    Localization:

         Improved various translations and clarified text with added tooltips.


Thank you for reading, and as always, I appreciate your feedback!

notes.title: Release notes 18 october 2024

This update brings a few new additions alongside the usual set of bug fixes and quality-of-life improvements:

 When holding something in your hand, pressing the right-click (pan button) will make the hand zoom to the ground to gently drop the object or character.

     Reworked lightning powers to include lightning strikes and storms.
     Revamped the power wheel to manage more icons without overlap.
     Improved the Ark event with VFX to help locate the lid and move it back to the island if it’s too far away.
     In the villager list, added a button to grab a villager and an indicator for active quests.
     Added an indicator on the power button to show if you need to hold the power or not.

     Added separate quality settings for shadows and anti-aliasing.


Bug Fixes:


     Fixed an issue where the hand gets stuck when displaying the menu from the villager list screen.
     Fixed the fire quest not working when the character has 100% fire resistance.
     Prevented the avatar from attempting to charm or enrage creatures immune to conditions.
     Added error handling to all line traces when spawning enemies to avoid defaulting to the center of the island.
     Added a limit to the number of fields that can be spawned at once to prevent filling the space with hundreds of unused fields.
     Fixed an issue where villagers would try to grab armor without actually taking it. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to reproduce the bug, but I tried to fix it—please let me know if it happens again.

Thanks for reading, and as always, don’t hesitate to provide feedback.

I clearly underestimated the number of messages I had to write, so some may lack inspiration. If you have any suggestions for helpful or snarky messages, feel free to share them with me!

Changes:


     Reduced the frequency and strength of certain events based on population size, making it easier to recover from sudden population loss.
     Reworked fireworks to increase the area of effect during the day.

     Reduced the size of altar fires to prevent villagers from setting themselves on fire while praying.

Thanks for reading, and special thanks to everyone who helped identify these issues or suggested improvements. If you have any feedback or encounter new problems, don’t hesitate to contact me directly.

notes.title: Release notes 13 september 2024
notes.content:
Hello,

Given the number of issues, I’ve integrated BugSplat for easier bug reporting in case of a crash. I’ve activated the crash reporter, so when the game crashes, you should see a window prompting you to submit a report. If you choose to submit, it will upload the crash files automatically. Please note that the crash report includes your hardware information, should you prefer not to share it.

I tested this locally, but unfortunately, I was unable to test it in the release version—you never seem to get a crash when you need one!

Additional Updates in This Release:


     Enabled Virtual Textures: This may help stabilize the game for resolutions higher than 1080p. However, it may trigger a full shader recompile when the game starts.
     Disabled Hardware Ray Tracing: Instead of allowing the engine to decide, ray tracing is now disabled by default.
     Bugfix: Addressed the issue where the ground would turn grey when shader painting (only on new islands).
     Bugfix: Resolved the issue where new forest/field sometimes didn’t spawn. Added a camera movement to the location, so the player can see it.
     Bugfix: Prevented the loss of resources when reloading a game.
     Bugfix: Adjusted the Initialization sequence to kickstart the navigation mesh creation. This should reduce or prevent characters from getting stuck at the beginning while waiting for navigation data.
     Bugfix: The maximum size of the avatar has been reduced to Improve movement and interaction within the town, 
     Bugfix: Adjusted the sound attenuation for worm death sounds to be more appropriate.


Thanks for reading! As always, don’t hesitate to provide your feedback.

notes.title: Early access Release
notes.content:
Greetings, aspiring gods!

I am thrilled to invite you to the early access of "Genesis of a Small God"! Here are the new features and improvements in store for you.

If you already tried the demo/previous playtest, I encourage you to try from scratch and reset the game in the options menu before trying this early access. Keeping previous saves may lead to unexpected behavior.


⚖️ Balance:  Add more fall damage/impact damage
🏢 New Buildings: The lighthouse allows warnings for incoming random events, while the kiosk enables villagers to play music, introducing a new job for bards.
✨ Rework the ice powers
🎨 Small Graphical Improvement and slight animation cleanup and more variety in sound effects
 🌏new language chinese; japanese; korean ; norwegian; polish; portuguese; russian; swedish as well as some UI improvement and fixes discovered while doing the translations.
🐞 And essentially A lot of bug fixes reported during playtests and (Probably) few new Bugs


What's the plan for the early access ?
There are still a few physics issues and optimizations that need to be addressed. Additionally, I plan to add a couple more buildings focusing on coastline interactions, such as the fisher pier. I have several ideas for additional random events to incorporate. Furthermore, the current distribution of random events is mostly random, and I aim to improve it to minimize player frustration.
But the main goal is to gather your valuable feedback to improve the game. Are there any cool powers you think could be interesting to add? Or new types of events to challenge the player? And yes I know everyone wants the big monster to educate like in black and white but it's not easy to make ;)

I appreciate your time and effort in helping me making Genesis of a Small God the best it can be. Thank you for your support, and I look forward to hearing from you soon on Discord or in the steam forum. 

Best regards,
Pierre Nury

notes.title: Open Playtest #5
notes.content:
Greetings, aspiring gods!

I am thrilled to invite you to the fifth open playtest of "Genesis of a Small God"! Here are the new features and improvements in store for you.

If you already tried the demo/previous playtest, I encourage you to try from scratch and reset the game in the options menu before trying this playtest. Keeping the same save may cause issues.


Gameplay:

Hand Throwing Rework: Modification of the hand throwing mechanics for improved consistency and bug fixes.
Harvester Role Improvement: Harvester now focus on filling the pantry and other buildings. Characters can now carry more than one item at a time.
Tutorial Messages: New tutorial messages have been added for Grab Power and Horn of Plenty. And new Visual effects confirm the validity of plant positions.
New Quests: No spoiler.
Random Events: No spoiler.
New Powera: Animal Transformation, Tornado, Blizzard, and Stalactite powers have been added.
Game Balance: Fall and impact damage have been adjusted for balance.
Stuck Detection: Characters now detect when they are stuck, triggering relevant quests.



Audio:

New Sound Effects: Animals now have unique sound effects, enhancing the overall audio experience.
Audio Grab/Ungrab: Audio cues have been added for object grabbing and releasing.


Visual:

Character Customization: Heretic characters now have distinct visual elements (mask and cape) to differentiate them from standard villagers.
UI: The Character UI has been modified to reflect the faith state of characters.
Powers: Sphere projections have been added to hands.


Technical:

Physics Enhancements: Ragdoll physics have been improved, ensuring smoother character animations and interactions.
AI Behavior: AI movement has been optimized to reduce wasted actions. Characters will now avoid some of the unnecessary movement.


Bug Fixes:

Various Fixes: Multiple bug fixes have been applied, addressing issues with AI behavior, power animations, and game mechanics.


I am looking for your valuable feedback to improve the game. Are there any cool powers you think could be interesting to add? Or new types of events to challenge the player? And yes I know everyone wants the big monster to educate like in black and white but it's not easy to make ;)

I appreciate your time and effort in helping me making Genesis of a Small God the best it can be. Thank you for your support, and I look forward to hearing from you soon on Discord or in the steam forum. 

Best regards,
Pierre Nury

notes.title: Open Playtest #2
notes.content:
Greetings, aspiring deities and divine enthusiasts!

I am thrilled to invite you to the open playtest #2 of Genesis of a Small God. This event will run for a week starting on June 9th, providing you with an access to my lastest build of the game.

If you already tried the demo/previous playtest, I encourage you to try from scratch and reset the game in the options menu before trying this playtest,

🌟 Main differences with the previous playtest:

 New Random Events: I added a dozen new events type and increased the number of events to 2 per season (customizable in option menu). These unpredictable occurrences will challenge your decision-making skills and add thrilling twists to your divine journey.
 Reworked Tutorial: I understand the importance of a solid foundation in mastering the art of godliness. Based on feedback on the previous playtest i reowrk the tutorial to be less disruptive while providing the necessary information at the beginning.
 Bug Fixes: I worked, addressing pesky bugs and technical issues reported during previous playtest. Probably introduce a few new ones, and i am compting on you to notify me of any issue you may faced.


I am looking for your valuable feedback to improve the game. Are there any cool powers you think could be interesting to add? Or new types of events to challenge the player? And yes I know everyone wants the big monster to educate like in black and white but it's not easy to make ;)
Additionally, I would appreciate your input on whether you think the game is ready for early access.

I appreciate your time and effort in helping me making Genesis of a Small God the best it can be. Thank you for your support, and I look forward to hearing from you soon.

Best regards,
Pierre Nury

The first version of the demo is now live. It contains 2-3 hours of gameplay:


 Buildings a simple village.
 Basic powers like fireball/rain/heal/reap are implemented.
 Terraforming powers for modifying the voxel terrain.
 2-3 random events that I won't spoil here.

 A bunch a animals.


What's next ? I am hoping to release an early access with a lot more content. You can see in the demo upgrade menu, the blueprint for the next powers to come. Fell free to suggest other on the forum. 
Also more building types and production chain for the village, as well as new random events to make each game unique.

Thanks for trying the game.
Pierre Nury
